mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced household wealth and lower equity demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not statistically significant at p < 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that feeds into higher wage growth and inflationary pressures, which in turn erode corporate profit margins and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% month-over-month indicates an acceleration in economic activity that boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the positive rank IC is below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary regime that increases risk premia and reduces equity attractiveness, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not significant at p < 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 900,000 units for three consecutive months signals weakening residential investment and consumer confidence, which correlates with lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month indicates a statistical artifact of labor force reclassification and does not signal genuine labor market strength; under these conditions, S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days are expected to be near-zero, with no directional bias.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are significantly negative (rank IC < 0.05) or significantly positive (rank IC > 0.95) in more than 40% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals reduced household buffer capacity and increased borrowing, which in a high-debt environment amplifies recession risk and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not significant at p < 0.01.
